title: BMW F 900 GS Sport arrives in Brazil for R$79,990 with an 895cc twin-cylinder engine producing 90 hp, a six-speed transmission with Shift Assistant Pro, an Akrapovič exhaust, heated grips and keyless ignition - CPG Click Oil and Gas
content: BMW Motorrad launched the F 900 GS Sport in Brazil, a new version of its middleweight adventure motorcycle, at a promotional price of R$79,990. The announcement was made on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Specifications are available in the BMW Brazil press release, published in São Paulo. Motonline and Motociclismo Online covered the motorcycle in detail on Tuesday, November 24, and also list its price, engine and equipment. Dafra launches new-generation SYM Joyride 300 scooter in Brazil with a 278-cc, 26-hp engine, LED headlights, ABS and unchanged R$27,990 price with freight included Hyundai Tucson GLS 2016 priced below a new Renault Kwid: 146-hp engine and 528-liter cargo area list at R$58,317 in FIPE Seven-seat Fiat Freemont fits the whole family and costs less than a brand-new Renault Kwid: the 2016 SUV, with a 172-hp 2.4-liter engine, automatic transmission and 580-liter trunk, is listed at R$62,000 in the FIPE table Nissan Versa SV 1.6 CVT 2017: Offers a 460-liter trunk and automatic transmission for less than a new Kwid The video above is from the MOTOO channel and was posted on August 5, 2024. It takes a detailed look at the 2025 F 900 GS, the model on which the Sport version is based. For Brazilian riders, the new model comes standard with Pro Riding Modes and Shift Assistant Pro. BMW Motorrad says the version makes the GS lineup more accessible in Brazil. The R$79,990 price is a promotional launch price, according to BMW Motorrad. The same offer is listed by Motonline, Motociclismo Online, Vrum and MOTOO. The F 900 GS Sport is available in Brazil in a single color: blue. The press release places the version in the Adventure segment and says its configuration strengthens the model’s competitiveness. The motorcycle comes with a three-year warranty. The term is stated in BMW Brazil’s official release and is also listed by Vrum, MOTOO and Motociclismo Online. The manufacturer says the Sport’s arrival is part of a strategy to maintain a diverse lineup. Its stated goal is to serve different types of riders and attract new customers. The engine is an 895cc liquid-cooled inline twin with eight valves. It produces 90 hp at 6,750 rpm, according to BMW Motorrad. MOTOO, Vrum and Motociclismo Online report the same 90 hp at the same engine speed. Motonline lists both power and torque at 6,750 rpm. Outside Brazil, the F 900 GS has a different engine tune. A global BMW press release dated September 7, 2023, lists 77 kW, or 105 hp, at 8,500 rpm. The same figure appears in a test published by U.S. magazine Cycle News on July 19, 2024: 105 hp at 8,500 rpm. BMW Motorrad presents the Sport version’s package as a combination of performance, efficiency and versatility. It is designed for both long highway trips and off-road stretches. BMW Motorrad’s U.S. account posted an image of the middleweight GS lineup on X on January 29, 2024. The post says the three motorcycles are ready for their next adventure: the F 900 GS, F 900 GS Adventure and F 800 GS. It then asks readers which one is their favorite. United by the #SpiritOfGS, the #F900GS, #F900GSAdventure and #F800GS are eager for their next adventure! Which one is your favorite?#HungryForMore #BMWMotorrad #MakeLifeARide pic.twitter.com/9dexMp8awy — bmwmotorradusa (@BMWMotorradUSA) January 29, 2024 The official torque figure is 93 Nm at 6,750 rpm, the same engine speed at which maximum power is reached. The figure appears in BMW Brazil’s announcement and the company’s 2023 global announcement. Brazilian websites converted the torque figure to kilogram-force meters, with differing results. Motonline reported 9.3 kgf·m, MOTOO listed 9.4 kgf·m, Motociclismo Online used 9.48 kgf·m, and Vrum gave 9 kgf·m. Car Blog and the Motor Mais website use the manufacturer’s 93 Nm figure. BMW Motorrad’s figure is the reference value. In the United States, Cycle News lists torque in pound-feet: 68.6 lb-ft at 6,750 rpm. That is the same engine speed listed in the Brazilian specifications. The transmission has six speeds. Shift Assistant Pro, BMW Motorrad’s shift assistant, comes standard on the F 900 GS Sport. The system allows riders to shift up and down without using the clutch, depending on operating conditions, Motociclismo Online explains. Motonline describes the same clutch-free use of the transmission. Motonline says Pro Riding Modes and the shift assistant are the features the Sport adds to the F 900 GS. The site describes them as more performance-oriented. Pro Riding Modes are standard equipment. In its 2023 global announcement, BMW says the F 900 GS has Rain and Road modes, ABS Pro and DTC traction control. The same announcement says the Pro package adds extra modes and mode preselection. It also includes engine drag torque control and Dynamic Brake Control, or DBC. The bike has a TFT display with connectivity through BMW Motorrad Connected, which links the motorcycle to a phone. The screen measures 6.5 inches, according to BMW’s global announcement and Vrum, which reviewed the Pro version in July. On the Duas Rodas magazine channel, journalist and rider Leandro Mello tests the F 900 GS in a video dated April 17, 2026. He evaluates the engine, riding modes, suspension and ergonomics. The Akrapovič muffler comes standard on the F 900 GS Sport. It is listed in BMW Motorrad’s announcement, MOTOO, Vrum and Motociclismo Online. Heated grips and hand guards are standard equipment. The lighting is full LED. The bike has keyless ignition through the Keyless system, which Motonline calls a proximity key. In its 2023 global announcement, BMW lists Keyless Ride as a factory option on the F 900 GS. Motonline says the standard F 900 GS already comes in Brazil with a proximity key, suspension adjustment, heated grips and an Akrapovič muffler. In the official Sport equipment list, the Akrapovič muffler appears alongside Pro Riding Modes and Shift Assistant Pro, all listed as standard equipment. The Sport’s suspension offers preload, compression and rebound adjustment. The brake and shift levers are adjustable. Both features are mentioned in BMW Motorrad’s announcement and in articles by Motociclismo Online, Vrum and MOTOO. On the F 900 GS Pro, BMW uses the Enduro Pro package. It includes a fully adjustable Showa front fork, a ZF/Sachs rear shock, a black handlebar with a riser and an M Endurance chain. Blue is the only color available in Brazil. Motonline calls the shade Snapper Rocks Blue and describes some of the bodywork in that color, a black base and a white rear frame. BMW Motorrad’s press photos show the F 900 GS Sport with a blue fuel tank and side panels, a black seat, a light-colored subframe and an Akrapovič muffler on the right side. In Brazil, the Sport is priced below the F 900 GS Pro São Paulo Yellow. BMW Motorrad launched the Pro on July 20, 2026, at R$93,990. Vrum reported the same price for the Pro on July 21, 2026. Both versions use an 895-cc engine rated at 90 hp and 93 Nm in the Brazilian specifications. The Pro adds the Enduro Pro package and a tall windscreen. The F 900 GS Sport is available for a promotional price of R$79,990 and comes standard with the Pro Riding Modes electronics, Shift Assistant Pro and a three-year warranty. BMW Motorrad’s global account on X highlighted its F 900 GS Adventure sibling on March 12, 2024. The post, written in English, says the motorcycle offers full touring capability in Thailand or the Black Forest, on mountain roads or highways. Whether in Thailand or the Black Forest, high mountain passes or highways, the F 900 GS Adventure delivers perfect touring capability. Get more details:➡️ https://t.co/yl5Y62umup #MakeLifeARide #SpiritOfGS #BMWMotorrad pic.twitter.com/oYNz6tnY3y BMW says the F 900 GS Pro is built at the BMW Group factory in Manaus, in the Brazilian state of Amazonas. The information appears in the brand’s July 20 and 23, 2026, releases. Vrum reported on July 21 that the F 900 GS Pro had begun production in Brazil. The Pro São Paulo Yellow was displayed at Capital Moto Week in Brasília from July 23 to August 1, 2026. The Sport is the family’s newest option in Brazil. BMW Motorrad describes the R$79,990 price as a promotional launch price. The F 900 GS Sport comes in blue and adds an Akrapovič muffler and heated grips to its standard equipment. title: Tommy G’s Clubhouse to serve Pensacola adults 22+ with disabilities at no cost - WEAR-TV
content: PENSACOLA, Fla. -- For many families who have loved ones with special needs, finding a place where they can socialize is often a challenge. A new space in Pensacola aims to change that. It's called Tommy G's Clubhouse, and it's being built specifically for adults 22 and older with intellectual disabilities. From arts and crafts, video games, a sensory room, a computer lab, and a library, Tommy G's Clubhouse will serve as a space where people with disabilities and their caretakers can connect free of charge. "Not everybody can work; not everybody has the capability to go in and do a four- or five- or eight-hour-a-day job, but they still need something to do," co-owner of Tommy G's Clubhouse Keith Grayam said. "They need a place to belong. We don't want them sitting at home and watching TV or playing a game system or just wishing they could be somewhere. So that's what's important about here." "He is 40 years old and operates at about a seven-year-old level. For a long time, I was a single father," Grayam said. "Wishing that I had some place to take my son other than just out for a drive or walking at the mall." That's how the concept of a special needs social and learning space was formed. "We are actually taking this room and turning it into a studio apartment," Grayam said. "We're going to help teach life skills in here. We'll have a bed in here, a stove, and a refrigerator." "Our friends can come in and work on making the bed and folding clothes and learning how to do the day-to-day chores that they're expected to do at home, too," he added. Co-owner Helen Rasberry says adults with special needs often age out of school programs by 22 and suddenly find themselves with fewer opportunities to connect with others. "We've just learned in the last year and a half that there are just not enough services out there for those with special needs," Rasberry said. "They can't necessarily participate in all of the things that everyone else participates in, and there are holes in the system, and people fall through." Before purchasing the building, clients enrolled in Tommy G's used to go on social outings together -- bowling, shopping, and interacting. "When we decided we needed a building, we thought we would find something small and just have a place for ourselves," Grayam said. "Then Helen was driving down the road and saw this building and called me, and we came in and went, 'Okay, we're not ready for this, but let's take a leap of faith and jump.' And that's what we did." The clubhouse will also have an enclosed outdoor yard with a sensory swing and outdoor pizza kitchen.

title: GS vs. C: Which Bank Stock Deserves a Spot in Your Portfolio? - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results The U.S. banking industry is benefiting from resilient dealmaking activity, robust trading revenues and growing demand for wealth and asset management services, despite lingering macroeconomic and interest rate uncertainties. Against this backdrop, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS and Citigroup, Inc. C stand out as two prominent banking giants well-positioned to capitalize on these favorable industry trends. While Goldman is leveraging its investment banking dominance, strong trading franchise and expanding asset and wealth management business to drive earnings growth, Citigroup is focused on business simplification, operational efficiency and strengthening its core banking, services and wealth franchises to improve profitability. With both banking behemoths pursuing distinct growth strategies and enhancing shareholder value, which stock offers a more compelling investment opportunity at present? Goldman has long maintained a leading position in mergers and acquisitions (M&A), trading and capital markets. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has strategically shifted away from non-core consumer banking operations to focus on its core strengths in investment banking (IB), trading, and asset and wealth management (AWM). These efforts continue to yield favorable results, with Global Banking & Markets revenues rising 34% year over year to $41.72 billion in the first nine months of 2026, supported by a 40% increase in IB fees, a 57% surge in equities revenues and a 6% rise in fixed income, currency and commodities (FICC) revenues. A rebound in M&A activity, robust underwriting volumes and sustained client engagement are expected to support the segment's growth, though a modest decline in the IB fee backlog as of September 2026 compared with December 2025 warrants monitoring. Goldman has been actively reshaping its portfolio through strategic acquisitions and divestitures. In August 2026, GS agreed to acquire LCN Capital Partners and NEOS Investments, strengthening its alternative real estate investment capabilities and expanding its presence in options-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs), respectively. These followed the acquisitions of Innovator Capital Management in April and Industry Ventures in January. Further, the divestiture of its Polish asset management business and the planned transition of its Apple Card program to JPMorgan Chase underscore Goldman's commitment to streamlining operations and directing resources toward higher-return businesses. Goldman's growing AWM franchise remains a key pillar of its long-term growth strategy. As of Sept. 30, 2026, assets under supervision reached a record $4.10 trillion, marking the 35th consecutive quarter of net inflows into long-term fee-based assets. The company is also aggressively expanding its private markets presence, targeting $300 billion in alternative credit assets by 2028 and $750 billion in total alternative assets under supervision by 2030. Additionally, its strategic partnership with T. Rowe Price to broaden access to public and private market investments should help diversify recurring fee-based revenues and reduce reliance on cyclical businesses. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as another important catalyst for Goldman's operational efficiency and profitability. Through its AI-driven operating model, One Goldman Sachs 3.0, the company is integrating automation across client onboarding, lending, risk management, regulatory reporting and other operational functions. Its collaboration with Anthropic to develop AI agents for complex internal processes further underscores its technological ambitions. Over time, these initiatives are expected to enhance productivity, improve operating leverage and support margin expansion. Unlike Goldman, Citigroup is undergoing a more comprehensive business transformation. Under CEO Jane Fraser, the company is advancing its multi-year strategy to simplify operations, improve profitability and focus on its five core businesses — Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards. These efforts are yielding favorable results, with revenues rising 12% year over year to $73.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Management expects revenues to see a 4-5% compound annual growth rate through 2026 Citigroup is nearing the completion of its multi-year exit from non-core international consumer banking operations. As of September 2026, the company had sold consumer banking businesses in 10 markets, exited two through wind-down activities and substantially completed its exit from South Korea. Following the sale of a 22.6% stake in Banamex in April 2026 and an additional 1.4% stake in August, C's ownership in the Mexican business declined to 51%. Management expects to deconsolidate Banamex in 2027, followed by an initial public offering (IPO), subject to market conditions and regulatory requirements. These divestitures should unlock capital for reinvestment in higher-return businesses, including IB and wealth management. Cost-cutting remains another major pillar of Citigroup's profitability improvement strategy. The company's headcount declined to 217,000 as of Sept. 30, 2026, from 227,000 a year earlier and 219,000 at the end of June 2026. Beyond workforce optimization, management is pursuing structural efficiencies through process simplification, platform consolidation and increased automation. Driven by these initiatives, the company now expects its efficiency ratio to be below 60% in 2026 and within 55-60% in 2027-2028, before declining below 55% over the medium term. Citigroup continues to invest in technology and AI to strengthen operational resilience, improve productivity and support revenue growth. The company plans to deploy an incremental $5 billion in strategic investments through 2028, primarily targeting technology modernization, marketing, front-office talent and branch renovations. Management is accelerating approximately $500 million of these investments into the second half of 2026. Further, C's improving earnings power and operational efficiencies are supporting enhanced shareholder returns. The company now expects a return on tangible common equity (RoTCE) of above 11% in 2026, up from its previous target of 10-11%, and is targeting 11-13% in 2027-2028 and 14-15% over 2029-2031. Over the past six months, shares of Goldman and Citigroup fell 19.7% and 9.7%, respectively, compared with the industry's decline of 3.3%. In terms of valuation, Goldman is currently trading at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of 10.87X. Meanwhile, Citigroup's stock is trading at a forward P/E of 8.75X. Both are trading at a discount compared with the industry average of 11.46X. However, C is cheaper than GS stock. C and GS reward their shareholders handsomely. Following the Federal Reserve's 2026 stress test, GS increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share beginning in the third quarter of 2026. Similarly, Citigroup announced a 12% quarterly dividend increase beginning in the third quarter, subject to board approval. C has a dividend yield of 2.4% while Goldman has a dividend yield of 2.5%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for GS' 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates increases of 39.3% and 3.4%, respectively. Over the past month, earnings estimates for both years have remained unchanged. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for C's 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates 43.5% and 14.6% growth, respectively. Over the past month, the earnings estimate for 2026 has been unchanged, while that for 2027 has been revised upward. While Goldman's IB leadership, robust trading franchise and expanding asset and wealth management business position it well for long-term growth, Citigroup appears to be a more compelling investment option at present. Its ongoing business simplification, disciplined expense management, strategic technology investments and improving profitability provide significant growth opportunities. Further, C's superior projected earnings growth, upward estimate revision for 2027 and attractive valuation strengthen its investment appeal. Despite execution risks associated with its ongoing transformation, Citigroup's improving return profile and potential for valuation expansion offer a more attractive risk-reward proposition. Hence, investors seeking stronger earnings growth at a discounted valuation may find C stock a better pick than GS at present. content: Genpact G stock has gained 20% over the past three months, against the industry’s 9.1% and the Zacks S&P 500 Composite’s 6.7% decline. Let us delve deeper into the factors contributing to the company’s outperformance. G’s Agentic Operations Drive Revenue & Margin Growth Genpact’s strategic transition toward Agentic Operations is expanding its addressable market, strengthening client relationships and creating recurring revenue streams. The company leverages its domain expertise and proprietary AI solutions to transform mission-critical business processes. Management expects Agentic Solutions bookings to comfortably exceed $1 billion in 2026, more than five times the 2025 level. New clients account for more than half of the cumulative awarded agentic contract value, underscoring Genpact’s expanding market reach. Meanwhile, the transition of existing clients to Agentic Operations is driving revenue growth and gross margin expansion. The shift toward multi-year, headcount-independent contracts should enhance revenue visibility, improve operating leverage and support long-term profitability. G’s Favorable Revenue Mix Fuels Margin & Earnings Growth Genpact’s shift toward higher-value technology solutions, disciplined pricing and operational efficiencies are improving profitability. Gross margin expanded for the 14th consecutive quarter, rising 160 basis points year over year to 38% in the third quarter of 2026. Revenues from headcount-independent contracts surpassed 55% of total revenues, reducing reliance on labor-intensive delivery models and enhancing operating leverage. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased 10.3% year over year to $1.07, outpacing revenue growth. Management raised its 2026 gross margin outlook to 36.9%, implying year-over-year expansion of about 90 basis points. Adjusted operating margin is expected to reach 17.7%, with adjusted EPS growth of at least 13%. Structural margin improvements should sustain earnings growth while providing flexibility to fund strategic investments. Genpact’s healthy liquidity position and disciplined capital allocation provide financial flexibility to pursue strategic investments and enhance shareholder value. The company ended the third quarter of 2026 with approximately $500 million in cash and cash equivalents. Operating cash flow totaled $93 million despite temporary invoicing and collection delays related to its Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) implementation. Collection trends recovered in October, with management expecting cash flow disruptions to normalize by early 2027. Genpact returned $62 million to shareholders in the third quarter, bringing year-to-date capital returns to $246 million. Management remains committed to its existing capital allocation strategy. Recovering cash collections and expanding profitability should strengthen cash flow generation, supporting continued investments and shareholder returns. Board Approved Bankruptcy Filing at Morning Meeting
Genesis PE to Pursue Main Lawsuit Energy Materials, a subsidiary of GS E&C (006360.KS), has decided to file for bankruptcy, and its second-largest shareholder, Genesis Private Equity, plans to take legal action. It is an unusual case of a major Korean conglomerate winding up through bankruptcy a subsidiary that had taken in funds from a financial investor, making a legal battle between the two sides unavoidable. Genesis PE will respond to the bankruptcy filing resolution with a main lawsuit, according to investment banking sources on the 26th. The firm is expected to argue that the bankruptcy filing approved by the Energy Materials board earlier that morning is invalid. Energy Materials plans to file for bankruptcy with the Daegu Bankruptcy Court. Its board consists of three directors representing GS E&C and one representing Genesis PE. Genesis PE had earlier sought an injunction to suspend the effect of a resolution to halt operations, and later filed a main lawsuit claiming the resolution was invalid. Its central argument is that the directors acted solely in the interest of GS E&C, the largest shareholder, failing to treat shareholders equally, and that there were procedural defects in convening the board meeting. The shareholders' agreement signed at the time of the investment required prior consent from Genesis PE for any suspension of business or dissolution and liquidation, but no separate consent procedure was carried out in this decision-making process, sources said. If the court declares bankruptcy, a trustee will liquidate the company's assets and distribute them first to creditors, leaving shareholders last in line. GS E&C became a creditor on the 13th of this month by repaying 112.5 billion won ($76 million) in Korea Development Bank loans on behalf of Energy Materials. The move was intended to prevent a chain default extending to the parent company's foreign currency bonds after Korea Development Bank signaled an event of default, citing deteriorating credit from the suspension of operations. Genesis PE set up a project fund in 2024 and invested 95 billion won ($64 million) in Energy Materials. The firm had built a friendly network with GS E&C through deals including the acquisition of stakes in GS Elevator and Xi Energy Operation, but the latest decision has soured relations between the two sides. "This case could worsen the capital market's perception of GS Group," an investment banking official said. Original reporting by Lee Young-ho for Seoul Economic Daily. AI-translated from Korean. title: GS Caltex Employees Pack 200 Winter Kits for Yeosu Residents - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
"Sharing Warmth" Volunteer Drive Heats Up Community Outreach
Employees Assemble 200 Winter Kits by Hand YEOSU — Employees of GS Caltex have gathered to help vulnerable residents in Yeosu who face both the winter cold and the burden of heating bills. The company said on the 26th that it held a "Sharing Warmth" volunteer event on the 25th at the conference room of the Yeosu City Community Social Security Council. About 30 employee volunteers took part and assembled 200 winter kits by hand. The volunteers checked and packed seven types of cold-weather items needed in winter, including thermal cushions, neck warmers, knit gloves, beanies, heat packs, KF94 masks and earmuffs. The kits contained more than just winter supplies. They also carried the employees' wish that their neighbors facing the cold months ahead would stay a little warmer. The completed kits will be delivered to older adults in vulnerable households and to families with members who have disabilities through the Yeosu City Senior Welfare Center, the Yeosu City Welfare Center for the Disabled and the Yeosu City Community Social Security Council. "It is a small gesture, but we hope it brings warm comfort to our neighbors in the community," a GS Caltex official said. "We will continue to look closely after those in need and carry on sharing with the local community." GS Caltex runs a range of community programs, including support for families in crisis through its "1,000-Won Happiness" small-donation campaign, the "Chuseok Sharing Warmth" drive and "Saerom Class," a program supporting the development of young people. title: Surily G’s Maharani edit turns pre-wedding occasion into an opulent expression of craftsmanship - IndulgExpress
content: Surily DP Goel’s contemporary Indian occasion wear label Surily G is famed for modern silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and distinctly feminine design language. Its new collection Maharani, the latest chapter of Surily’s five-part collection, Modern Heirlooms 2026, draws inspiration from the ornate artistry of the Baroque era and the timeless elegance of Victorian fashion. The outfits have an interplay of elaborate embellishments, rich textures and statement-making silhouettes. Intricate marodi embroidery enriched with delicate pearls, mirrors and gold accents lend depth and dimension to each ensemble. The collection balances ornate craftsmanship with contemporary silhouettes. A striking palette of black and gold, ivory and gold, alongside vibrant multicoloured combinations, further enhances its regal character. Surily takes us through the same. The idea was to explore the grandeur of regal dressing through a contemporary lens. I wanted to draw inspiration from the ornate artistry of the Baroque era and the timeless elegance of Victorian fashion, while interpreting these influences through my own design language. It is designed for the woman who enjoys dressing up, embraces individuality, and wants to make a statement at celebrations, particularly sangeet evenings. How different is this collection from your previous ones? Maharani has a more opulent and dramatic aesthetic compared to some of my earlier collections. It explores a richer design language, with a strong emphasis on marodi embroidery, elaborate embellishments and the influence of Baroque and Victorian fashion. While the collection has a distinctly regal character, it still retains the youthful, feminine and slightly unconventional sensibility that is central to Surily G. How did you balance the regal, structured weight of Baroque and Victorian aesthetics with the fluid ease required for a modern sangeet dance floor? For me, it was important that the garments felt as good to wear as they looked. While the inspiration is rooted in the grandeur of Baroque and Victorian aesthetics, I wanted the silhouettes to remain contemporary, feminine and easy to carry. We have explored a variety of styles, including shararas, kaftans, and corsets, allowing the collection to have a sense of drama without feeling overly restrictive. How did you reimagine marodi embroidery and enrich with modern elements like pearls, mirrors, and gold accents? Marodi embroidery forms the foundation of Maharani, and I wanted to highlight its intricacy while giving it a more contemporary expression. We brought in elements like pearls, mirrors and gold accents to add depth, texture and dimension to the embroidery. The interplay of these details enhances the richness of the garments while complementing the Baroque and Victorian influences that run through the collection. The intention was to celebrate the beauty of traditional craftsmanship while making it feel relevant to the modern woman’s wardrobe. How do you see today’s brides and wedding guests styling themselves nowadays? I think today’s brides and wedding guests are looking for a balance of style, comfort and sensuality. They no longer want to feel overly dressed up; instead, the focus is on choosing pieces that complement their bodies, with colours and silhouettes that reflect their personal style while allowing them to feel comfortable and confident. After all, they want to be able to enjoy the celebrations and dance the night away. I believe the key is to invest in one timeless statement piece that creates a sense of occasion, while keeping the rest of the look effortless and understated. Tell us about your design inspirations and personal fashion choices. My design inspiration comes from just about anything and everything. I don’t consciously seek inspiration; I think it is often absorbed subconsciously. It could come from nature, architecture, geometry or symmetry, or even my travels and the colours I encounter along the way. I find it difficult to pinpoint a single source of inspiration, as it is an ever-evolving process and something that continues to develop with my work. When it comes to my personal style, I am fortunate to be constantly surrounded by beautiful fabrics and intricate embroideries, so I tend to keep my own dressing relatively simple. I gravitate towards solid colours and understated looks, although I also enjoy experimenting with a more bohemian aesthetic. I like having the freedom to move between the two, depending on how I feel and how I want to express myself. What are some bridal and festive wardrobe must haves? A pre-draped sari, a beautifully structured corset, a statement jacket, a versatile dupatta and a draped skirt are key wardrobe staples. We still have two more chapters to unveil as part of Modern Heirlooms. The upcoming collections, Prism and Elan, will explore more cocktail and reception-focused dressing, with a range of pieces suited to celebratory occasions. title: New Economics of Retirement: What 2026 Retirement Data Means for Employers - Goldman Sachs
content:
We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. For decades, the employer retirement playbook was simple: offer a plan, drive participation, and largely have employees make the decisions from there. By that standard, many organizations are succeeding. However, Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Retirement Survey and Insights Report 2026 suggests that the playbook is now incomplete. "The retirement challenge facing Americans today is no longer simply participation or access," the authors write. In the report's introduction, Greg Wilson, Head of Retirement at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, and Chris Ceder, Senior Retirement Strategist at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, describe rising living costs as leaving workers with "less capacity to save for the future" and pressures they believe "threaten long-term retirement readiness." Company leaders have a mandate of serving employees while also protecting the organization. The report’s authors suggest framing financial wellbeing and retirement readiness as "a shared imperative rather than a private burden." Many surveyed employees are enrolled, contributing, and "doing what conventional wisdom tells them to do." Yet the share of working respondents who increased their retirement savings fell from 55% in 2025 to 39% in 2026. This is the largest single-year decline since 2020. That change was reported while the economy was expanding, equity markets delivered strong returns, and US unemployment stayed low by historical standards near 4%. With steady employment, strong markets, and high plan participation, why is self-reported retirement progress "deteriorating across every generation?" So, what's getting in the way? Workers suggest the issue is the competing financial demands they face every day. When asked to identify their biggest obstacles to saving, respondents cited housing costs (31%), day-to-day living expenses (31%), and debt payments (27%). The report’s authors observe that the more immediate priorities, including major milestones like buying a home, tend to come first, while retirement is "the easiest to push aside when nearer pressures crowd in." Since 2000, the cost of buying a home has risen from 33% of median income to 54%.1 That financial strain gets “absorbed quietly in the hours people work and the life goals they postpone." More than 60% of survey respondents say they have taken on work outside their primary job, mostly out of necessity, and nearly 70% have delayed a major financial goal. Where Employee Financial Stress May Appear in the Workplace Financial insecurity “is not contained within household budgets; it follows survey respondents into the workplace.” More than half of working respondents (53%) say financial concerns make it difficult to focus at work. Nearly a third (31%) missed work in the past 12 months because of a financial challenge, and 34% were likely to look for a new job primarily to improve their finances. That exposure is concentrated among early- and mid-career talent. The survey found financial security doesn’t uniformly improve with income. The survey finds a U-shaped pattern across several measures, with concerns declining through middle-income ranges before rising again among some higher-income respondents. Those earning above $300,000 report more distraction at work than those earning $100,000 to $300,000 (64% vs. 47%), and half say they are likely to look for a new job to improve their finances. While the nature of those concerns may differ by income level, financial wellbeing may not always be apparent from income alone. For employers, when pay and benefits don't ease the pressure, workers "may seek relief elsewhere." This is "a measurable workforce risk," one that touches retention, succession planning, and organizational continuity. "Given the impact financial stress can have on work quality and productivity, employers have a unique opportunity and clear incentive to provide innovative support tools beyond traditional retirement plans," said Jonathan Barber, Head of Compensation & Benefits Solutions at Goldman Sachs Ayco. Those tools range from financial wellness programs and debt management assistance to home-buying benefits and lifestyle spending accounts. For workers facing real constraints on how much they can set aside, the answer is not simply to save more. The findings point more toward three areas employers may consider, highlighted below: 1. Make personalized planning available to everyone with the help of AI Personalized advice "is no longer optional." Respondents with a personalized plan were more than twice as likely to say they're on track (72% vs. 33%). The top request, from 43% of respondents, is to help know whether they're on track and what to change if they aren't. Another 31% want help getting the most out of company-provided benefits, such as receiving the full employer match, where offered. New guidance tools can extend personalized planning to workers who have historically been hard to serve one-on-one. About half of respondents (51%) have used AI for retirement planning, but most still prefer a person for major life events (73%) and retirement income decisions (63%). The report positions AI as "an on-ramp," not a replacement for human advice. The report observed, "When the contribution cannot rise, the return potential of those contributions matters even more." A professionally managed portfolio with higher return potential tied with a personalized investment portfolio was the most requested 401(k) menu enhancement, each selected by 38% of respondents. The report points to interest in broadening the range of investment opportunities available to retirement savers, including access to private markets. Respondents indicated that professional management (40%) and access to an advisor (39%) would increase their comfort with private market exposure. Workers may know how much they've saved but not how much they can safely spend each month, or how long that money will last. That's why, as the report puts it, "a balance is not the same as a paycheck.” It describes retirement income solutions as one way to convert accumulated savings into "potentially higher and more durable monthly income.” Demand is broad: more than eight in ten respondents (83%) want at least some guaranteed income in retirement, and 59% of workers fear outliving their savings. Employment remains essential to retirement security, but for many workers, the report authors conclude, it is "no longer sufficient.” While "a structural problem is not a permanent one," solving the new dynamics of retirement will mean rethinking "how we save, invest, and support people at every stage of their financial lives." title: No-Reserve 1994 Acura Integra GS-R With Vertical Doors Was an Extra in '2 Fast 2 Furious' - Motorious

A 1994 Acura Integra GS-R hatchback on Bring a Trailer is listed with vertically opening doors, a Jackson Racing supercharger and a claim to 2 Fast 2 Furious screen time. It is being offered at no reserve, with bidding at $1,320 as of this writing and the auction ending Monday, November 30. According to the listing, the owner's late father bought the Integra in 1996 and the car was later used as an extra in 2 Fast 2 Furious. The seller says RavenWood Paint and Body applied the custom black-and-red paint in 2003 following filming. In the auction comments, the seller said he is helping sell the car for a family that lost its father. That film-era connection puts it in the same orbit as other cars from the franchise we have covered, including Paul Walker's 2 Fast 2 Furious Evo and the Petersen Museum's Fast & Furious anniversary exhibit. Unlike those, this one is a background player, and there is no film documentation described in the listing beyond the seller's account. Under the hood is the 1.8-liter DOHC VTEC four-cylinder, fitted with a Jackson Racing supercharger, an aftermarket intake and Comptech dress-up parts, plus a Comptech strut tower brace. Power goes to the front wheels through a five-speed manual transaxle. The listing does not state a horsepower figure. Underneath, the Integra rides on 19-inch HRE ten-spoke wheels wrapped in 255/40 Firestone Firehawk tires, with drilled and slotted rotors and SSBC Force 10 front calipers behind them. It is the kind of build that fans of the car's tuning culture will recognize from our look at the world's fastest Integra, though this one leans toward show-and-shine rather than record runs. The headline modification is the set of vertically opening doors, joined by a body kit, aftermarket headlights, a rear wing and a power sunroof. Inside, the black-and-red upholstery gets a Momo steering wheel and pedal covers, carbon-look trim, a Sony head unit and a Clarion screen. The cargo area holds Sony Xplod subwoofers, an amplifier and a CD changer, while auxiliary gauges sit on the driver's A-pillar and an A'PEXi V-AFC controller rides on the dashboard. The odometer shows about 72,000 miles. The listing says the car comes with the owner's manual, service records and an Arizona title, and the CARFAX report shows no accidents or damage. The seller notes that the air conditioning was serviced in October 2026 and that the turn signals do not self-cancel. The car is located in Peoria, Arizona. CARFAX lists a single owner, and the car has been offered by a private party. If you want more Integra reading while the bidding runs, our story on the Integra Type R that took on a G80 M3 shows the nameplate in a very different, modern light. In home cleaning and textile maintenance sectors, electrical safety, temperature rise control, and mechanical protection have become strict baseline metrics. Buyers no longer select products based solely on suction power numbers; instead, they examine how internal components withstand continuous operational stress. Within this shifting trade environment, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. (Amare) has established a robust operational foothold by aligning manufacturing precision with international safety expectations. As a specialized enterprise focusing on textile maintenance devices, Amare operates as a China leading carpet spot cleaning machine supplier, addressing the rigorous demands of global distribution networks through systematic quality control. The contemporary supply chain environment places considerable emphasis on verifiable reliability at the factory level. Retailers across Western Europe and North America scrutinize supplier credentials down to individual component tolerances and circuit board layouts. When sourcing a carpet spot cleaning machine, procurement teams look for manufacturers who can demonstrate consistent output without compromising on electrical insulation or thermal management. This operational reality requires production facilities to maintain tight tolerances during plastic injection molding, motor assembly, and wiring harness installation. By integrating advanced testing instruments directly into production lines, manufacturing plants can filter out potential defects before final packaging. The Significance of GS Certification in European Markets Quality assurance frameworks in export destinations rely heavily on recognized third-party safety marks. The GS mark, standing for Geprüfte Sicherheit, represents an authoritative German safety certification recognized throughout the European Union. Tested strictly against European Norm standards by accredited independent testing institutions, this mark verifies that a product meets statutory safety requirements regarding mechanical strength, electrical insulation, ergonomic design, and chemical composition. Although the GS mark is technically voluntary under European product legislation, major German retailers, DIY warehouse chains, and regional distributors treat it as a mandatory prerequisite for market entry. Compared to the CE marking, which relies primarily on manufacturer self-declaration, the GS mark requires factory inspections and independent laboratory testing of physical samples. This distinction makes GS certification a formidable benchmark for overseas suppliers seeking entry into premium retail channels. Retail buyers recognize that products bearing this safety mark have undergone rigorous evaluation regarding potential hazards such as short circuits, overheating, user burns, and toxic material emissions. Consequently, achieving GS compliance transforms a standard household appliance into a trusted consumer commodity. Manufacturers who invest in this certification demonstrate a long-term commitment to consumer protection and regulatory transparency, distinguishing their offerings in crowded retail environments. Meeting stringent German safety standards requires meticulous attention to engineering and internal component design. At its manufacturing facility in Zhejiang, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. implements dedicated engineering protocols to ensure that every device meets mechanical and electrical safety requirements. The company's core product lineup includes versatile 500W spot cleaning units engineered for deep textile extraction. These compact machines utilize proprietary self-developed water pumps and heating elements designed to balance cleaning efficiency with thermal stability during extended operation cycles. To prevent fluid ingress into sensitive electrical compartments, these 500W units feature a deliberate clean and wastewater separation architecture. The dual-tank configuration isolates fresh cleaning solution from extracted wastewater, preventing cross-contamination and reducing the risk of internal short circuits. Furthermore, integrated overflow prevention sensors automatically halt water intake when recovery tanks reach maximum capacity. Motor overheating protection mechanisms monitor operational temperatures in real time, cutting power supply automatically if thermal thresholds are exceeded due to restricted airflow or extended continuous use. Beyond internal fluid dynamics, the structural integrity of the appliance plays a critical role in mechanical safety. Precision metal and plastic molds ensure that housing components maintain exact wall thicknesses and tight assembly clearances. This dimensional consistency eliminates loose panel gaps where moisture or dust could penetrate internal circuitry. Strain reliefs on power cords and secure internal wiring harnesses prevent wire fraying or disconnection under mechanical vibration. By combining robust thermal management, precise fluid isolation, and durable mechanical housing, Amare ensures that its carpet spot cleaning machine achieves the structural reliability necessary to pass rigorous GS laboratory evaluations. A credible safety certification is only as reliable as the manufacturing consistency behind it. To maintain continuous compliance with European standards, export suppliers must implement comprehensive batch tracking and quality traceability systems. In modern factory operations, accountability extends from raw material intake to final packaging and palletization. Each manufactured unit receives a unique laser-etched serial number and production batch barcode, linking the finished appliance to specific material lots, component suppliers, and assembly shift logs. When independent auditors inspect production facilities for GS surveillance audits, they examine these traceability records to verify that mass-produced items match the exact specifications of the original tested prototype. Critical components such as thermostats, power switches, pump motors, and internal wiring cables are sourced from qualified tier-one suppliers with verifiable material test reports. Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. archives all incoming material inspection certificates and end-of-line electrical safety test logs in a centralized digital database. This rigorous documentation process enables channel distributors and retail buyers to trace safety data instantly if quality inquiries arise. If a specific batch requires verification, quality assurance personnel can retrieve electrical insulation test results, high-voltage breakdown test records, and functional test logs within minutes. This level of operational transparency reassures commercial partners that product safety is managed through systematic engineering protocols rather than random spot checks. Such structured traceability reinforces long-term trust between Chinese manufacturing enterprises and international trade partners. As international buyers raise expectations regarding electrical safety and mechanical durability, suppliers must anchor their operations in verifiable engineering standards. Amare has positioned itself at the forefront of this movement by embedding strict quality protocols into every stage of production, from raw material inspection to finished product testing. By mastering the technical requirements of GS certification, the company delivers reliable cleaning solutions that meet the exacting standards of European retailers and commercial distributors. title: How Hedge Funds Are Navigating Stock Market Volatility - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Hedge funds are reducing risk and hedging their portfolios with short positions amid volatility in technology stocks, says Vincent Lin, co-head of Prime Insights and Analytics in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. While “faster money” types, including hedge funds using momentum strategies, are being more cautious, "slower money" investment among retirement savers remains historically elevated. In The Markets podcast, Lin also highlights opportunities in hyperscalers and in defensive sectors like healthcare. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Monday, November 23rd, and I'm here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Vincent Lin, who is co-head of Prime Insights and Analytics within our FICC and Equities business. And today we're going to talk a lot about the hedge fund volatility, market volatility that's taking place, how hedge fund customers are holding up in this environment, and what's the path for the year ahead. Chris Hussey: Okay, Vinny, let's start with the volatile market that we've had because last week, big sell-off. This week, bouncing back a little bit. Amidst it all, a big spike in vol. What do you make of it? And more importantly, what are our hedge fund clients telling you is happening? Vincent Lin: If we take a step back, right, the performance backdrop within the overall hedge fund complex has become a lot more challenging the past few months. This was particularly true for the month of October, and I would say November month to date as well, coming into today. So, we have seen our hedge fund clients unwinding risk, so essentially degrossing activity for five straight weeks before last week. So, collectively, hedge fund clients have been paring back a lot of their net exposures and also gross exposures recently as well. I think what's changed last week is that even though the overall degrossing activity stopped, we actually have seen hedge fund clients become incrementally more cautious by adding shorts, right? So, they were in the market adding a lot of short positions across both single stocks and also macro products, meaning index futures and ETFs, so essentially the market hedges. For context, last week our hedge fund clients added ETF shorts by about 19 percentage points just in the past week, which would be the third-largest weekly increase we have seen in the past decade. So clearly, I think there's a lot of uncertainty and also fragile sentiment being expressed by our hedge fund clients. Chris Hussey: Yeah, very fragile sentiment. Obviously, that can be expressed with shorts. That can also be expressed with longs, though. What are they rotating into? What are you seeing our hedge fund clients rotating into? Vincent Lin: Yeah. So, if we look at the overall market on a sector industry level, right, sectors like consumer staples, utilities, and also REITs. Kind of the defensive sectors have meaningfully outperformed the market in the past month. Coincidentally, those are also the sectors that hedge fund clients have sold a lot less, right, versus say tech or the AI infrastructure space in the past month. And I think the reason being that obviously, those are defensive sectors carrying a lot lower beta versus the overall market, but they are also the sectors that are much less exposed to overall consumer spending, for example, as well as having low correlations to AI. Chris Hussey: Vinny, a lot of those defensive trades are also rate-sensitive trades. How much of this is a bet on rates? Vincent Lin: So, within the tech complex, we have seen our hedge fund clients gravitate toward the hyperscalers, which is obviously much higher quality in terms of balance sheet, in terms of their defensive characteristics with regards to earnings. And then secondly, on the short side, right? Our hedge fund clients actually have been actively shorting some of the more recessive pockets within the consumer space. For example, housing, including home builders. That's where I think positioning has been declining to pretty much multi-year lows on the PB book, and that's primarily driven by short additions. Chris Hussey: All right, let's back away from your hedge fund expertise, and I want to ask you about the retail investor, the individual investors out there, because over the course of 2026, we've seen that individual investor get very long and then pull back from the market and then get long again. Going into this, you got a sense that the individual investor was long again. How much of this volatility that we're seeing is being caused not by our hedge fund community, but individuals? Vincent Lin: If I can break up the positioning in terms of two cohorts, right? I would say fast money versus slow money. If I look at the fast money types, meaning hedge funds or CTAs, meaning momentum-driven strategies, their positionings are pretty close to either multi-year lows or toward the bottom end of the historical range. I'll argue some of the faster money retail kind of day trader types, we certainly have seen, you know, less enthusiastic trading activity in some of the more retail-driven pockets of the market in the past month. However, if I look at the slower money, meaning kind of the household 401K mutual funds type of accounts, a case can be made that their positioning is still fairly elevated versus history. In fact, if I look at, the overall ETF and mutual fund complex, collectively they have attracted $150 billion of inflows in the past month, and this is happening in the middle of the market drawdown. Chris Hussey: Yeah, no, very interesting. The households still own a lot of stocks. All right. Let me ask you about, a little bit about the Santa Rally, because you mentioned earlier that the hedge fund community was sort of going into this sell-off with poor performance overall. Does that set us up for a rally, or do you feel that they're going to fade any rally here? Vincent Lin: So, I think in historical periods when we see elevated macro uncertainty, particularly coupled with a lack of clarity in earnings outlook going into next year, I think there's a phrase being thrown around meaning buyers live higher, and I think this dynamic applies here, right? Both for the fundamental long short community because of the performance drawdown that we have seen in the past month, I think managers generally speaking, despite positioning already at this price levels, they want to see some more stabilization in market prices. Given the fact that there's not much time left toward the end of the year, I think our hedge fund clients are still more in a capital preservation mode than chasing the tape. And then secondly, if I look at the systematic, the momentum-driven community, our future strats model forecast is also calling for more constructive flows if price can stabilize from here or even trend higher. So, I think buyers live higher is what I would describe it. Chris Hussey: One last quick question around that. Is there anything that your hedge fund clients are seeing from a fundamental standpoint, or that is getting them to want to sell the market here? Either it is credit spreads widening or any element of that. Are you seeing anything? Vincent Lin: I would say and I know we'll touch on performance, but performance drawdown, it has been an issue. And typically, when you are not making money, your risk appetite, in terms of deploying more capital has been reduced. So, that's by far the biggest factor. The second one, I think, you know, from a fundamental perspective, the AI narratives have clearly gotten more challenging. And I think most of the sentiment or conversation we're having is that the best of the AI infrastructure returns is probably behind us. So essentially, the AI trade is starting to transition from, you know, kind of the AI infrastructure layer to the monetization and returns and the use cases of the AI infrastructure trade. And historically, especially, in the middle of this kind of as big of a technology cycle like we're in right now, the transition period is always the most difficult. Chris Hussey: Yeah. And so, let's touch on that performance element of it, because you mentioned it. Are hedge funds now in a good enough performance period where they can add risk, or do you feel like nah? Vincent Lin: Take a step back, look at first half of the performance. Obviously, our equity fundamental long-short clients in midyear, they were up a lot. About 17% on an asset-weighted basis. And like I mentioned, the last few month has been difficult because that cohort is the most exposed to the AI theme. But even after the recent drawdown, they're still up 7% coming into today. Vincent Lin: So down but not out is what we describe it. Also equally important, if I move away from the fundamental long-short cohorts, if I look at the performance of our systematic long-short clients, meaning quant equities, their returns actually have strengthened since midyear. So even though the fundamental long-short cohort have suffered a pretty sharp drawdown, there's still much more dispersion going around. And I think hedge funds collectively are still holding up. And then, I think one last thing I'll mention is we have noted in our past reports that hedge funds, really since COVID, have done much better versus a traditional 60/40 equity bond portfolio, and I think that dynamic is still intact. Chris Hussey: All right, Vinny, lots to digest here. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Vincent Lin: So within the tech and AI complex, I still like the hyperscalers. In the scenario that the compute capacities remains constrained, I think they will be relative winners. Also, if we do see evidence of AI CapEx growth start to decelerate meaningfully from here, the more positive free cash flow dynamic and generation is going to open up a lot more capital deployment possibilities, including share buyback. Within the defensive space, I like healthcare over staples. One, I think valuation is a lot more attractive. Also, secondly, there are multiple secular earnings drivers within the space that are also less exposed to AI. Chris Hussey: All right. Last question for you because we're going to be moving into December next week, and we'll have a whole new set of catalysts. Vincent Lin: So first of all, this week we'll have multiple late cycle tech reporters. I think those are going to be important to watch for kind of the latest spending on AI. And then secondly, I think for the remainder of this year, it's going to be dominated by macroeconomic prints, right? So, later this week we'll have PCE, next week we'll have payroll, and then three weeks from now we'll have the November CPI. I think those collectively are going to be important to gauge in terms of determining the Fed's next move, not only for December, but also going to next year. Is the more recently hawkish posture warranted, or can we see possibly some evidence of a dovish turn? Chris Hussey: Vinny, always a wealth of information. Thanks so much. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: FIRST RIDE | BMW F450 GS delivers accessible entry into adventure riding - Business Day
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the new F450 GS as its entry-level adventure motorcycle in South Africa. Replacing the single-cylinder G310 GS, it is a more powerful machine with a twin-cylinder 420cc engine and is BMW’s latest contender in the growing market segment of medium-displacement bikes. Like its larger stablemates in the GS range, it is a versatile all-rounder, combining everyday usability, touring comfort and off-road capability. Its more accessible price and manageable power output should appeal to beginners without disappointing more experienced riders. The bike’s tractable power delivery is one of the things that impressed me most when I rode it at the South African media launch in Gauteng earlier this week. On roads that took us along popular breakfast-run routes in Hartbeespoort, as well as on gravel trails, the engine felt punchier than I expected for its small size. The parallel-twin engine, with outputs of 35kW at 8,750 rpm and 43Nm at 6,750 rpm, proved to have a free-revving nature that gave the medium-sized bike a zesty spring in its step, whether pulling off or overtaking slower traffic. With a top speed of around 170km/h, it has good touring potential too, and the small screen provides decent wind protection at higher speeds. With claimed fuel consumption of 3.8l/100km, the bike has a range of more than 350km on its 14l tank. The engine has a single balance shaft to reduce vibrations and it’s mostly effective, though I felt some buzzy vibrations through the seat at certain revs. The unit has a characteristically fruity twin-cylinder sound without being too noisy. All versions of the bike except the basic version have a quickshifter, which allows clutchless up- and downshifts in the six-speed transmission. Standard on the GS Trophy and optionally available on the other variants is an Easy Ride Clutch (ERC). Using a centrifugal clutch, it allows you to operate the bike without the clutch lever, even when pulling off, but allows the rider to intervene manually at any time if necessary. It is packed with much of the technology found in its more expensive stablemates, including standard traction control, engine drag control, heated grips and lean-angle-sensitive anti-lock braking The F450 GS is a mid-sized bike that won’t feel too intimidating to novice riders. Weighing 178kg, it is a lot smaller and wieldier than the big daddy R1300 GS, which tips the scales at a portly 238kg, but retains the typical GS sense of heft and solid feel, with high-quality finishes. Available in three saddle heights to accommodate various-sized riders, the 450 is also unmistakably a GS in design, with its distinctive flyline, tough-guy looks, and features such as an LED headlight with an “X” daytime riding light. It is also packed with much of the technology found in its more expensive stablemates, including standard traction control, engine drag control, heated grips and lean-angle-sensitive anti-lock braking. All models have three riding modes — Rain, Road and Enduro — with an additional Enduro Pro mode from the Exclusive model upwards. The latter disables the ABS assistance on the rear wheel, allowing the rider to lock the wheel deliberately when necessary on gravel, giving greater control over braking. On off-road sections of the route, the F450 GS excelled with its comfortable ride and reassuring agility. I was particularly impressed with how yielding the suspension was and how effectively it absorbed bumpy, rippled surfaces. There was no chance to test it in soft sand, but on rough gravel the middleweight BMW displayed the classic GS turf-taming ability. Wider enduro footrests are included from the Exclusive version upwards or are available as optional accessories. The front wheel is guided via KYB upside-down telescopic forks, while the rear wheel has a double-arm swingarm with a KYB central spring strut featuring progressive damping. The Sport and GS Trophy variants feature sports suspension that allows the rider to adjust both rebound and compression damping. All but the base model have handguards and wide off-road footrests, while the range-topping GS Trophy has an aluminium engine guard. The brakes comprise a single 310mm front disc with a Brembo four-piston fixed caliper and a single 240mm rear disc. The F450 GS comes standard with aluminium alloy wheels (19-inch front and 17-inch rear), but is optionally available with more trail-focused spoked wheels. The dual-purpose Maxxis tubeless tyres provided good grip both on and off the tar. The 6.5-inch TFT display is legible in sunlight and menus are accessed via an iDrive-style rotary controller. There is a USB-C socket, and taking phone calls, listening to music and using navigation while riding are all possible via smartphone and helmet pairing. title: NBA Power Rankings: Whom is each team most thankful for this year? - ESPN
content:
As the NBA plays its final games Wednesday night before the Thanksgiving holiday, there is plenty to celebrate around the association as the first full month of the season winds down. MVP front-runners Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama have jumped out to sizzling starts, adding to their already impressive résumés as they lead the Los Angeles Lakers and San Antonio Spurs to the top two spots in the West. Meanwhile, Doncic's former Lakers teammate LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers have surged to the top of the East. The Miami Heat are certainly grateful to be the winners of the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes, riding a seven-game win streak after dropping their first four games of the season. And the Portland Trail Blazers have welcomed Damian Lillard back with open arms, coming off a blowout win over James and the Sixers on Monday night. In this week's Power Rankings, our insiders rank each of the 30 teams and also highlight one player, coach or executive each team should be thankful for as we celebrate Thanksgiving -- with some lamb chops and gravy, of course. POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Next games: @ POR (Nov. 25), vs. LAL (Nov. 27), vs. BOS (Nov. 29), @ MIL (Nov. 30) In switching to the current guard-heavy starting lineup, San Antonio needed to find ways to optimize the group around franchise superstar Victor Wembanyama. What better way to do that than by bringing in a veteran assistant in Hall of Famer Donovan, who has extensive expertise in that area? Throughout his head coaching tenure in Oklahoma City, Donovan worked with a bevy of dynamic guards such as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Russell Westbrook, Chris Paul and Dennis Schroder, and understands how to make the spacing work with so many perimeter players on the court together at the same time. The Spurs' new lineup isn't a finished product yet, but the addition of Donovan is helping it round into form quickly. -- Michael C. Wright Next games: @ SA (Nov. 27), @ MEM (Nov. 29), @ HOU (Nov. 30) The 27-year-old supernova is on the short list for the way-too-early MVP contenders (shoutout to our former colleague and current Atlanta Hawks front office member, Tim Bontemps) and has been electric to watch this season, averaging a career-best 36.6 points. It's not only Doncic's scoring that has been a boon for L.A. as it has stayed atop the Western Conference standings. Doncic's sturdy defense -- more recently as a roamer in the Lakers' full-court zone defense and throughout the season with his one-on-one containment (he is second in the NBA in charges drawn) -- caused one team source to tell ESPN that Doncic has been playing "the best defense of his life." -- Dave McMenamin Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 25), @ IND (Nov. 27), @ HOU (Nov. 28), vs. MEM (Dec. 1) The Sixers play in front of one of the NBA's most passionate fanbases, but also one of its most scorned. It has been 43 years since the Sixers' last title, and for the past decade they endured the infamous tanking era, massive injuries and years of heartbreaking second-round exits. James' signing gave this fanbase real championship hope after years of disappointment. And his impact has been felt early, as the Sixers are off to their best start since 2000-01, which happens to be their most recent finals appearance. -- Kris Rhim Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 25), vs. MEM (Nov. 27), @ SAC (Nov. 29), @ POR (Dec. 1) The Timberwolves didn't officially sign Kuminga until September, months after most of this summer's free agents found new homes. But the long wait has been worth it for both sides: With Minnesota buying time for Anthony Edwards to return from knee surgery, Kuminga has provided valuable contributions on both ends. The athletic forward has averaged 13.4 points and shot 39.7% on 3-pointers in a complementary offensive role, and he's part of a well-balanced starting lineup that has posted an excellent plus-10 net rating without Edwards. -- Ben Golliver Next games: vs. PHX (Nov. 25), vs. PHI (Nov. 28), vs. LAL (Nov. 30), vs. TOR (Dec. 1) Perhaps it's too early to attribute Amen Thompson's shooting improvements to Houston's decision to bring in shooting guru Engelland as an assistant, but you can't discount his track record and reputation around the league, where he's widely regarded as the NBA's best shooting coach. Engelland has worked in the past with Grant Hill, Tony Parker and Kawhi Leonard, along with all of Oklahoma City's young core players, and the results speak for themselves. Thompson should become the latest beneficiary of Engelland's tutelage, along with Reed Sheppard, Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason. -- Wright Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 25), vs. MIA (Nov. 27), vs. ATL (Nov. 29), @ CHI (Dec. 1) The Knicks look like themselves again, and one big reason has been Towns' consistency. He has had a double-double in every game and leads the NBA in rebounding (13.9). He's playing through the uncertainty of his future as the contract situation hangs over him and the franchise all season long. Still, his shooting splits are ridiculous: 21.8 points on 54/42/76. If there's a reason the Knicks can be counted on to repeat, he's atop the list. -- Vincent Goodwill Next games: @ PHI (Nov. 25), @ NYK (Nov. 27), @ CLE (Nov. 29), vs. ATL (Dec. 1) Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo's MVP-caliber start to the season, we would be remiss to not mention Riley as the person Heat fans should be most thankful for. The list of players Riley has drafted, traded for or signed in Miami is a who's who of current and future Hall of Famers: Alonzo Mourning, Dwyane Wade, Shaquille O'Neal, LeBron James, Chris Bosh, Bam Adebayo, Jimmy Butler and now Antetokounmpo. Miami has won three NBA championships and reached the playoffs in 24 of Riley's 31 seasons with the franchise as head coach and later head of basketball operations. title: GS Group elevates fourth-generation founding family member to president as stability anchors reshuffle strategy - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The conglomerate promoted GS Retail CEO Hur Suh-hong to president while retaining major affiliate chiefs and expanding its next generation of executives. GS Group promoted Hur Suh-hong, a fourth-generation member of its founding family and CEO of GS Retail, to president on Wednesday, while keeping the chief executives of its major affiliates in place. The 2027 reshuffle covers 40 executives: two promotions to president, four new CEOs, six promotions to senior executive vice president, four to senior vice president and 24 newly appointed vice presidents. Unlike last year, when GS replaced the CEOs of nine affiliates, this year's reshuffle prioritized management stability and business continuity. Hur Suh-hong is the eldest son of Samyang International Chairman Hur Kwang-soo, a cousin of GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo. Huh and Hur are different spellings of the same Korean surname. Hur Suh-hong worked at GS Energy and GS Holdings before becoming CEO of GS Retail. As head of the future business team at GS Holdings, he led the group's acquisition of botulinum toxin maker Hugel, which helped diversify its businesses. Since taking the helm, Hur Suh-hong has focused on strengthening GS Retail's core businesses and on transforming its operations through AI. GS Retail posted record quarterly consolidated revenue and operating profit in the third quarter this year, helped by record convenience store sales and sharply higher operating profit at its supermarket and home shopping businesses. The recovery in its core businesses and improvements to its business structure are seen as the reasons behind his promotion. Lee Tae-hyoung, the chief financial officer of GS Holdings and head of its portfolio management team, was also promoted to president. Born in 1970, he started out as an engineer at the Yeosu refinery of Honam Oil Refinery, now GS Caltex. He later served as head of corporate planning at GS Energy and CEO of Incheon Total Energy Company, a GS Energy subsidiary. Lee Tae-hyoung was credited with keeping the group's finances sound while supporting its search for new businesses such as AI data centers. He will now coordinate investment priorities and funding plans to back Chairman Huh Tae-soo's growth strategy. Other fourth-generation family members also took on bigger roles. Huh Joo-hong, a GS Caltex executive, and Huh Chi-hong, head of GS Retail's strategy division, were both promoted to senior executive vice president. Huh Joo-hong is the son of Huh Myung-soo, a standing adviser at GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C), and Huh Chi-hong is the son of GS Caltex adviser Huh Jin-soo. Huh Joo-hong will head GS Caltex's chemicals and lubricants division, which oversees its petrochemical and lubricant businesses. Huh Chi-hong will coordinate GS Retail's companywide strategy and look for growth through overseas business and investment. GS also promoted executives who delivered results in the field and in management. Kim Ki-hwan of GS Energy has led its renewable energy and new business strategy, and Kim Young-ju of GS Caltex pushed for more efficient operations and digital transformation at its production sites. Kang Yoon-seok of GS Retail helped improve the company's earnings structure, and Sung Nag-hyun of GS E&C has three decades of procurement experience. All four were promoted to senior executive vice president. GS kept the CEOs of its major affiliates but nominated new chief executives for four energy and power generation subsidiaries. Kim Jin-hak was tapped for Incheon Total Energy Company, Lee Jong-jin for GS Gumi Combined Heat and Power Plant, Heo Chang-ik for GS Donghae Electric Power and Yeo Seung-sub for GS Banwol Combined Heat and Power Plant. The appointments are seen as a response to changes in the electricity market and an effort to keep the subsidiaries' power plants running reliably. The group also stepped up efforts to develop its next generation of leaders. GS named 24 new vice presidents, a 33.3 percent increase from 18 in each of the previous two reshuffles. Eight are in their 40s. GS E&C named 10 new executives, double the number in its previous reshuffle. The appointments span its core housing and urban redevelopment businesses as well as future growth areas such as property development and data centers. GS EPS put a new vice president in their 40s in charge of the future business division at its power policy headquarters. "With uncertainty high at home and abroad, we chose stability so that our major affiliates can carry on with the business innovation they have been pursuing," a GS official said. "We will continue to support each affiliate in strengthening the profitability and competitiveness of its core business and in finding new growth engines through cooperation among affiliates, so that they can deliver tangible results." Korea's pay-TV subscriber base fell for a second straight year, while Internet Protocol TV (IPTV )users rose to more than 60 percent of the market. Roh Soh-yeong rejected Chey Tae-won’s proposal to pay the full divorce settlement within a week, disputing its delay and no-lawsuit terms. Jay Puri’s marriage to former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen has drawn attention amid a probe into alleged China-bound chip smuggling. The company has placed memory development under new leadership and expanded system LSI sales and marketing to accelerate next-generation AI chip technologies.

title: GS Retail CEO Promoted to President After Record Quarter - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
