Focus on "fundamentals" drove six straight quarters of profit growth Huh Seo-hong, chief executive of GS Retail (007070), has been promoted to president two years after taking the top job, a move seen as recognition within the group for driving growth at the convenience store chain GS25, the supermarket chain GS The Fresh and the home shopping network GS Shop, including six consecutive quarters of year-on-year operating profit gains. GS Retail said on the 25th that Huh was promoted from executive vice president to president in GS Group's regular executive reshuffle for 2027, announced the same day. The promotion comes two years after he became chief executive of GS Retail in 2025. Since Huh took office, GS Retail has posted year-on-year increases in operating profit for six straight quarters, from the second quarter of last year through the third quarter of this year. In the third quarter, the company posted revenue of 3.31 trillion won ($2.3 billion) and operating profit of 132.1 billion won ($91 million), its best quarterly results on record. Since becoming chief executive, Huh has emphasized management focused on fundamentals, including strengthening the core business and pursuing profitable growth. One example is his push for a so-called scrap-and-build strategy at GS25, aimed at lifting sales at existing stores rather than expanding the store count. Existing stores were relocated to better nearby locations, and the company added more stores with expanded fresh food sections to target demand for grocery shopping close to home. The number of such stores roughly doubled to 1,074 in September this year from 557 at the end of 2024. These stores, which carry a wider range of fresh produce, fruit and meat, generate about 1 million won more in daily sales than regular outlets. GS25 posted record revenue of 2.47 trillion won ($1.7 billion) in the third quarter. GS The Fresh, the supermarket chain, expanded mainly through franchising and raised the share of quick commerce to 10.1%. Third-quarter revenue reached 527.7 billion won ($364 million), topping 500 billion won for the first time in a quarter. The number of stores rose to 608 at the end of September this year from 531 at the end of 2024. GS Shop, the home shopping unit, has logged four consecutive quarters of year-on-year improvement by expanding differentiated products, including building Core Authentic into a fashion brand with annual orders of 100 billion won ($69 million). In a corporate value enhancement plan for 2026 announced in August, GS Retail set a medium- to long-term target of 380 billion won ($262 million) in operating profit by 2028. "We plan to focus first on strengthening the core competitiveness of our convenience store, supermarket and home shopping businesses through management centered on fundamentals," a GS Retail official said. "We will gradually flesh out our blueprint for new businesses and expanded overseas operations to achieve sustainable growth." Huh is a fourth-generation member of the family that controls GS Group. He began his career in 2002 as an analyst in the corporate finance division of Samjong KPMG. He joined the new business team at GS Home Shopping in 2005, worked at Chevron and GS Energy from 2009, and headed the future business team at GS Holdings in 2020. He served as head of the management strategy service unit at GS Retail in 2023 before becoming chief executive in 2025. Original reporting by Kim Heung-rok for Seoul Economic Daily. title: Energy Materials Moves to Shut Down; No. 2 Shareholder Threatens Legal Action - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Genesis PE, Which Invested 95 Billion Won, Pushes Back
Confirmed Liquidation Would Send Shockwaves Through Capital Markets This article appeared on Signal, a capital markets service, at 1:42 p.m. on Nov. 25, 2026. GS E&C (006360) is moving to shut down Energy Materials, its battery recycling subsidiary, following an indefinite suspension of operations last month. Genesis Private Equity, the second-largest shareholder in Energy Materials, has begun legal action, calling the move a unilateral decision made without its consent. The case could effectively wipe out the private equity firm's investment at the hands of a large corporate group, a prospect expected to send ripples through the capital market. GS E&C has settled on closing Energy Materials and plans to convene the subsidiary's board this week to approve the decision, according to investment banking sources on the 25th. Energy Materials, a GS E&C subsidiary, had been running large losses amid a weak market and falling metal prices. Genesis PE has escalated its legal action against Energy Materials. Early this month it filed for an injunction to suspend the effect of the suspension resolution, and it subsequently filed a main lawsuit arguing that the board resolution approving the shutdown was invalid, according to sources. The firm is understood to believe that the directors served only the interests of GS E&C, the largest shareholder, failing to treat shareholders equitably, and that there were procedural defects in convening the board meeting that decided on the suspension. Industry officials say that if the closure is confirmed, Genesis PE will find it difficult to recover its investment. Even if liquidation proceeds, GS E&C, now a creditor, would be paid first. Some point out that a precedent in which a large group winds down a subsidiary that had taken outside investment, leaving the investor with losses, could also dent confidence in GS Group across the capital market. The Energy Materials board had earlier voted last month to offer voluntary retirement to all employees and to suspend operations indefinitely. The Korea Development Bank then issued notice of a planned event of default, citing credit deterioration from the suspension, and GS E&C repaid 112.5 billion won in KDB loans on behalf of Energy Materials. The concern was that the subsidiary's loans could trigger a chain of defaults on the parent company's foreign currency bonds. Genesis PE invested 95 billion won in 2024 to acquire convertible preferred shares in Energy Materials. GS E&C currently holds 77.65% and Genesis PE 22.35%. The shareholders' agreement signed at the time of the investment is said to have required Genesis PE's prior consent for any suspension of business, dissolution or liquidation. There have been cases in which financial investors backing large corporate groups saw returns fall short of expectations or struggled to exit, but it is rare for a decision by the invested company itself to inflict large losses on the investment. "Large groups have shouldered as much of financial investors' principal as possible, driven less by the numbers than by a desire to preserve the trust of the market and institutional investors," an investment banking industry official said. "This decision will set a bad precedent for investing alongside large groups." Original reporting by Lee Young-ho for Seoul Economic Daily. AI-translated from Korean. title: Speaker G S Patil summons Forest officials over elephant relocation row - Deccan Herald
content: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly G S Patil has summoned officials of the Forest Department for a meeting on Wednesday to discuss the relocation of elephants from Belur in Hassan district to the Bhadra Tiger Reserve Chikkamagaluru after legislators from the latter district threatened to resign over the development. Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office on Monday in a sign of protest. However, she did accompany Chikkamagaluru MLA H D Thammaiah and Tarikere MLA G H Srinivas to the meeting with Patil, who was apprised of the situation. Motamma said that the Speaker was convening a meeting of the Forest Department officials and four MLAs, including Sringeri MLA T D Rajegowda, whose constituency will also be impacted by the relocation operation. "The Speaker was surprised to learn that the foresters had undertaken the operation without taking the legislators, planters' association and farmers into confidence," Motamma said. Accusing the Forest Department of entirely disregarding the safety of the people of Chikkamagaluru, Motamma asked, "Who will be held responsible for any loss of life during the operation? What is the guarantee these relocated elephants will not stray into human habitats later." Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who is currently touring Japan, is learnt to have spoken to the Chikkamagaluru legislators, and asked them to keep their resignation in abeyance, while promising them that the issue would be resolved. "The CM has instructed the Forest Department to put the operation on hold till he returns to Bengaluru on Wednesday night," said Motamma. Disputing the foresters' claims that the elephants had moved to the Bhadra Tiger Reserve of their own accord, Motamma said, "They were driven there to ease the pressure on the forest in Hassan. But our district is already grappling with human-animal conflict given that there are around 400 elephants in the region." Meanwhile, KPCC president B K Hariprasad urged Nayana Motamma to reconsider her decision to resign, saying the issue would be resolved through discussions with the government. He said the MLA had agreed to hold back her resignation for now and that a decision would be taken after the chief minister returns from Japan.

title: GS Caltex Seoul KIXX Tops First Round With Four-Game Streak - 조선일보
content: Coach Lee's strategic moves, including captain Yu Seo-yeon's third-set entry, and key players' performances secure victory [Daejeon = Sports Chosun Lee Jong-seo] GS Caltex Seoul KIXX advanced through the first round in first place. GS Caltex defeated Jung Kwan Jang Redsparks of the HK Savings Bank 2026–2027 V-League women’s division 3–1 (25–21, 28–30, 25–16, 25–13) in a first-round match held at Chungmu Gymnasium in Daejeon on the 24th. GS Caltex recorded 5 wins, 1 loss, and 15 points with a four-game winning streak, taking first place ahead of Korea Expressway Corporation Hi-Pass (5 wins, 1 loss, 15 points, set ratio 2.500) in set ratio. Before the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, “Reducing our reliance on Silva, who has always been a constant for us, worked well. Our blocking wasn’t great, so we focused heavily on serves. The serves went in well, which helped the blocking. The momentum from winning the Cup tournament carried over, which was fortunate, even though we prepared during the off-season.” The positive atmosphere continued. GS Caltex was led by Silva (22 points), Tanacha (19 points), and Choi Ga-eun (15 points), who all scored in double digits. Although they had regrets after losing the second set in a deuce, they prevented the momentum from shifting in the third set and successfully secured all three set points. After the match, Coach Lee said, “Overall, we handled things well. The opponent’s serves were strong, but we held our ground. If we had lost the second set after going to deuce, the momentum could have shifted, but the players maintained good focus in the third set and turned things around.” Despite losing the second set, Coach Lee focused on encouraging the players rather than showing impatience. He said, “We lost the second set narrowly, but I told them their performance wasn’t bad. There were one or two critical moments, and since it was an away game with young players, they looked flustered, so I urged them to stay calm. I told them to stay positive because their performance was coming together.” The decision to start captain Yu Seo-yeon from the third set, who wasn’t in the starting lineup for the first and second sets, proved effective. Coach Lee said, “When Seo-yeon enters the game, the team stabilizes in terms of attack, defense, and connections. As the captain, she leads well when the momentum is swinging. I put her in with that in mind.” Choi Ga-eun’s performance, who tied her personal best with 15 points, brought a satisfied smile. Coach Lee said, “She’s doing well. I praise her appropriately, but when things go well, getting overexcited can backfire. I give her light feedback to help her manage her emotions. She has bright energy, but sometimes she rushes. I talk to her about that.” GS Caltex, which finished the first round in first place, will begin the second round against Hongkuk Life on the 27th at Incheon Samsan Gymnasium.

title: Japanese Stocks Are Projected to Rally Again in the Coming Year - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The Japanese stock market’s gains this year have been driven largely by the banking and artificial intelligence (AI) sectors. Goldman Sachs Research expects the performance to broaden going forward, particularly because of the government’s push for corporations to use their cash to invest in growth. As long as capital expenditures in AI are ongoing, Japanese equity earnings per share (EPS) are forecast to increase again in fiscal year 2027—though at a more modest pace, Bruce Kirk, chief Japan equity strategist, writes in a report. Goldman Sachs Research projects the TOPIX of Japanese equities to rally about 20% to 4,500 in the next 12 months (as of November 24), based on estimates for growth in EPS of 9% in fiscal year 2027. “We believe that 2027 will be a transitional year for the Japanese equities market,” Kirk writes. The main drivers of Japanese stock gains for the past three years have been AI and normalization by the Bank of Japan. In 2027, Kirk expects investors’ tactical diversification into less crowded positions and less volatile themes, combined with the government’s market-wide efforts for corporations to invest sensibly in future growth, to produce a shift in the factors propelling the market. Communications from Japan’s Tokyo Stock Exchange; the Financial Services Agency; the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry; and the Takaichi administration suggest “a well-coordinated shift in top-down pressure towards promoting the use of excess cash reserves to drive the future growth initiatives across corporate Japan,” Kirk writes. “Growth” is the key word in Japan's corporate governance reforms, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “This should lead to a re-focus of interest on corporate governance-related themes in 2027, but skewed more towards growth investment and corporate restructuring,” Kirk writes. Our strategists have argued that improvement in return-on-equity at the index level will require “more drastic corporate structuring measures” than have taken place so far. These measures include mergers and acquisitions, operating segment restructuring, and consolidation. “This is where we think investor interest will shift towards in 2027,” Kirk writes. Goldman Sachs Research notes that, despite recent improvements, the TOPIX's return on equity still lags behind a wide range of markets globally. One of the best ways to address this gap would be to promote sector consolidation via increased levels of domestic mergers and acquisitions, Kirk writes. Prime Minister Takaichi's growth strategy highlights 17 strategic sectors and 62 key products and technologies. The strategy is designed to promote investments that enhance resilience against potential crises and promote growth, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “Without secure and reliable access to energy, power generation, natural resources, critical minerals, and rare earths, most of the other growth strategies will become almost impossible to achieve,” Kirk writes. As part of a $550 billion trade deal between the US and Japan, a number of power generation and energy security-related projects have already been approved or announced. “We see significant overlap between the Japanese government's energy and resource-related initiatives and future partnership opportunities with the US administration,” Kirk writes. Kirk identifies five key themes for investors in Japanese equities in 2027: AI innovation and quality: Goldman Sachs Research’s framework for AI-related stocks sorts them into two core groups: the AI semiconductor ecosystem and the AI data center hardware ecosystem. While the correlation between the two groups is “extremely high,” Kirk points out that AI companies in this dataset that scored highly in terms of innovation and quality significantly outperformed those that scored lower between April 2025 and June 2026. Corporate restructuring: Japan's new corporate governance code focuses on "growth-oriented governance." It urges corporate investment that supports sustainable mid- to long-term growth. It also stresses fair treatment of minority shareholders during mergers. Goldman Sachs Research expects a significant rise in takeover bids, management buyouts, and industry consolidation from 2027 onward. Physical AI: Labor costs for non-financial TOPIX companies reached 10.5% of sales in fiscal year 2025, up from 8.5% in fiscal year 2016. This is the highest level in a decade, excluding distortions during Covid. Goldman Sachs Research analysts forecast that humanoid robot prices, meanwhile, will decline from about $42,000 in 2025 to $21,000 by 2035. The government’s strategy aims for the deployment of 350,000 AI robots by 2030 and about 10 million by 2040. Energy and resource security: Japan imports almost all of its oil, natural gas, coal, and critical minerals. Its energy self-sufficiency fell from 22% in fiscal year 1998 to 6% after the shutdown of the Fukushima nuclear power station in 2011. While that figure recovered to 16% by 2024, Japan remains highly vulnerable to supply disruptions. The government's growth strategy aims to diversify sources of minerals and raw materials; secure energy supplies; strengthen the production supply chain for components; and expand solar, thermal, and advanced nuclear power. These plans could benefit trading companies, shipping firms, energy companies, and heavy industry. Cybersecurity: Japan's growth strategy explicitly prioritizes security products and services suited to the AI era, including support for domestic technology development and adoption. The government aims for domestic cybersecurity companies to generate annual revenue of more than 3 trillion yen ($18.8 billion) by 2035. title: This Acura Integra GS-R For Sale Is The 2 Fast 2 Furious Car Of Your Dreams - CarScoops
content: It's supercharged, dripping in red, and selling with no reserve. The Nissan Skyline, Mazda RX-7, and Toyota Supra were far from the only beloved Japanese sports cars used throughout the Fast and Furious franchise. During the first film, two Acura Integras were used, including one driven by Mia Toretto, played by Jordana Brewster. As it turns out, an Integra GS-R also served as an extra in "2 Fast 2 Furious" and is now up for auction in the U.S. The Bring a Trailer auction doesn't note if the car had any screen time, but documents from filming in 2002 show the production company behind the film was charged $2,472 for damage to the Integra's front and rear bumpers and grille. The year after serving as an extra, the car was repainted in a combination of black and red. This Integra certainly isn't as cool as Brian O'Conner's Nissan R34 Skyline GT-R, but it will be a lot more affordable, so it has that going for it. Contrasting the exterior paint is a set of 10-spoke 19-inch HRE wheels clad in 255/40 Firestone Firehawk tires. The Acura also includes a set of upgraded drilled-and-slotted brake discs and SSBC Force 10 calipers. It's under the hood where even more significant upgrades have been made. The original 1.8-liter inline-4 now includes a Jackson Racing supercharger and an aftermarket air intake. The listing doesn't make any mention of how much power the car has, though it's safe to assume it should be pretty sprightly. Drive is sent to the front wheels through a five-speed manual transmission. The engine bay also looks the part of a dramatic show car. It includes bright red hoses throughout, several chrome accents, and a red Comptech Sport strut bar. The wild red theme continues into the cabin, where the seats are trimmed in red and black, and there are red floor mats, a red instrument cluster, and red on the Momo steering wheel. There are also several carbon fiber accents inside, as well as an aftermarket audio system. An Integra like this is obviously an acquired taste and won't appeal to everyone. But for anyone who grew up wanting a "2 Fast 2 Furious" build, it ticks almost every box, and it's being offered with no reserve, so it might end up going for cheap. This generation of Integra, which spawned a Type R that sold for $204,000, is also well regarded for its handling, so while the exterior and interior are a little bold, it should be plenty of fun to drive.

title: Starting Chess at 39 to Winning 3 Asian Medals for India: Ezhilarasi G’s Journey - ChessBase India
content: For most competitive players, turning 39 marks a step back from the tournaments, but for Bengaluru-based Ezhilarasi G., it was the beginning of an extraordinary journey. Affected by polio at the age of three, she discovered structured chess during the COVID-19 lockdown and, within four years, represented India at the 4th Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities in Bishkek, winning one silver and two bronze medals. In her own words, she shares how determination and support turned a childhood pastime into an international podium finish. My name is Ezhilarasi. I am 43 years old, originally from Nathamalai village in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, and currently residing in Bengaluru, Karnataka. I was affected by polio at the age of three, resulting in a physical disability affecting both my legs. Due to my circumstances, I had to discontinue my formal education after Class 8. Growing up in a small village, I had very limited exposure to the outside world. From the age of 14 until around 30, I spent most of my time at home. During my childhood, as I was not attending school, I started playing chess at home with my brother. At that time, I had no idea that chess could offer opportunities beyond simply playing a game. Gradually, I developed a special interest in it, little knowing that it would one day become such an important part of my life. Later, due to personal and family circumstances, I left home and started working with NGOs. I learned embroidery, handicrafts and other creative skills, and eventually began teaching these skills to persons with disabilities. During my work with an NGO in Chennai, I met my husband, Adarsh Edamana, at the age of 31. We got married two years later, in 2016, and eventually settled in Bengaluru. My husband has always been my biggest strength, encouraging me to pursue my dreams and supporting me through every difficulty. My serious chess journey began at the age of 39 during the COVID-19 lockdown, when I started playing again at home. I decided to learn the game properly. Since travelling to a training centre was difficult, my first coach, Karthik, came to my home and trained me for around three months. Later, I met with an accident and suffered a fracture in my right hand, but I did not give up chess. I came to know about the Chess Federation for Physically Disabled (CFPD), which supports persons with disabilities through chess. In December 2022, I participated in my first national-level competition at Tumakuru. There, I met Mr Anand Babu VL, Secretary of CFPD, who encouraged and supported me in participating in tournaments and selection events. I also met Coach NI – Dinakaran B, who has been training and guiding me ever since. Their support has played an important role in my progress. In 2024, I participated in the Tata Steel 4th All India Specially Abled FIDE Rated Chess Championship, held in Jharkhand, and secured first place in the Unrated Category with 5.5 points. I qualified for the 2nd Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities 2024, held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. I scored 6 points out of 9 rounds and secured fourth place in the women's championship. After that, I participated in a few national and international tournaments but could not achieve the results I had hoped for. However, I continued participating, learning from every experience and working to improve my game. In May 2026, I participated in the Chief Minister Trophy – 6th CFPD National Chess Championship 2026, held in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, from 27 to 30 May 2026. I secured 2nd Position (Silver Medal) in the Wheelchair Women (WC-Women) category. This achievement paved the way for my selection by the Sports Authority of India (SAI) to represent India internationally. My biggest achievement came when I represented India at the 4th Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities, held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, from 29 October to 8 November 2026. Being one of the nine players representing India was a proud moment. I was also the only woman representing Karnataka and the only woman above 40 years of age in the Indian contingent. I won three medals for India: Silver in Women's Rapid Chess and Bronze in Women's Blitz and Women's Standard (Classical) Chess. Standing on the international podium and representing my country was an unforgettable experience. I am deeply grateful to my husband, Adarsh Edamana, Mr Anand Babu VL, Secretary of CFPD, for his encouragement and support, Coach Dinakaran B for his continuous training and guidance, and Mr Tamil Arasan, our team manager, for supporting us and taking care of the arrangements throughout the championship. My journey has also involved financial difficulties. After COVID, my husband lost his job, making it challenging to manage household expenses and support my chess career. Due to financial constraints, I could not participate in as many tournaments as I wanted. Nevertheless, we have managed with whatever resources we have and continued supporting my chess journey. At present, I teach chess to a few children at home, helping them learn the game from the basics. This provides me with a livelihood while allowing me to share my knowledge and love for chess. Alongside teaching, I continue to train and prepare for upcoming competitions. My dream is to keep improving, participate in more international competitions and win gold medals for India. I also hope my journey inspires other women and persons with disabilities to pursue their dreams, irrespective of age or circumstances. I began my serious chess journey at 39, and today, at 43, I have represented India and won three medals at an Asian Championship. For me, chess is no longer just a game I played with my brother; it has become a journey that has changed my life. I believe it is never too late to start something new, believe in yourself, and achieve what once seemed impossible.
